clue.text: Copyist requiring directions about illicit translation

indicators.note: the compass points go about, or around, the crib in this clue

parts.note: S and E, south and east, are two compass directions
a crib is a translation used, often illicitly, by a student

explanation.surface: A copyist needs guidance on an illegal translation.
explanation.definitionFit: A scribe was a professional writer who copied documents by hand.

clue.text: Distinct part

definitions.meaning: distinct as an adjective: apart, not joined
to part is to divide or move asunder

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means apart and distinct; as a verb it means to divide.

clue.text: It's ludicrous to get annoyed about little brother or sister

indicators.note: the irritation word goes about, around, the sibling word here

parts.note: to rile someone is to get them annoyed
sib is a short form of sibling, a brother or sister

explanation.surface: It is silly to lose your temper over a younger sibling.
explanation.definitionFit: Laughable and ludicrous are synonyms.

clue.text: Have second thoughts and support course of action

parts.note: to back is to support
a track is a course or line of action

explanation.surface: Someone changes their mind and endorses a plan.
explanation.definitionFit: To retreat from a position or opinion after rethinking it is an idiom for having second thoughts.

clue.text: Poignant work of spirit

definitions.meaning: poignant, as of a melody that lingers movingly in the mind
what a ghost does when it visits a place

explanation.definitionFit: A tune can be movingly memorable, and a ghost's visiting of a house is the same word.

clue.text: A burden shouldered by management, affecting everyone

indicators.note: in a down clue the burden sits on top of the management, as if carried on its shoulders

parts.note: a cross to bear is a burden
the board is the management of a company

explanation.surface: Management carries a burden that touches the whole workforce.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for applying to all, equally and without exception.

clue.text: Prickly type of enemy?

definitions.meaning: an enemy is, read as two words, no friend at all

explanation.definitionFit: The nopal is a Mexican prickly-pear cactus; split in two the word says not a friend, which is what a foe is.

clue.text: Complaint involving bad head

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill luck
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness

explanation.surface: A complaint that includes a terrible headache.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint is a medical disorder or ailment.

clue.text: Lines up in entrance to go for a spin

indicators.note: the reversed lines are placed in the entrance word

parts.note: a gate is an entrance

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: RY, railway, gives the crossword's lines

explanation.surface: Railway lines lead up to a gateway where someone sets off for a drive.
explanation.definitionFit: To gyrate is to whirl or revolve, to spin round.

clue.text: Conflicts famous for historic bloomers on both sides

definitions.text: Conflicts famous for historic bloomers on both sides

parts.words: Conflicts famous for historic bloomers on both sides
parts.note: fifteenth-century English civil wars where each side, York and Lancaster, took a flower as its emblem

explanation.surface: Wars remembered for embarrassing historical blunders by each side.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloomers suggests gaffes, but here means flowers: the white rose of York and red rose of Lancaster.
explanation.definitionFit: These dynastic wars are named for the flower badges of the two royal houses.

clue.text: Urge president to provide early transport

parts.note: to push is to urge
a chair presides over a meeting

explanation.surface: Lobby the chief executive to lay on transport in good time.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby buggy is the first vehicle a person rides in, early in life.

clue.text: River bird mostly living in the Arctic

parts.note: the Po is the great river of northern Italy

indicators.note: most of the bird's name is kept, its final letter dropped

parts.note: a lark is a songbird

explanation.surface: A river bird's habitat is mainly the far north.
explanation.definitionFit: Polar describes anything belonging to the regions round the North or South Pole.

clue.text: Refunds royalty to English novelist

parts.note: R stands for rex or regina, king or queen
H. E. Bates was an English novelist

explanation.surface: A novelist hands back royalty payments.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebates are partial repayments, money given back.

clue.text: Way to trap foreigner in angle of fortification

indicators.note: the street abbreviation catches the foreigner inside it

parts.note: ST, street, is a way
an alien is a foreigner

explanation.surface: A road is used to ambush an outsider at a bastion's corner.
explanation.definitionFit: In military architecture a salient is a part of a fortification jutting outward to an angle.

clue.text: In jest he taunted a character in Athens

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words of the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a Greek figure as a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet, used in Athens.

clue.text: One doesn't believe a lot can be changed

definitions.text: One doesn't believe a lot can be changed

parts.words: One doesn't believe a lot can be changed
parts.note: a person convinced events are predetermined, so that one's lot in life is fixed

explanation.surface: A sceptic doubts much can ever be altered.
explanation.walkthrough: A lot can be changed looks like an anagram signal over A LOT; here lot means destiny.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a person holds that fate rules everything and nothing can alter it.

clue.text: In Long Island, timid person going around in posh car

parts.note: LI abbreviates Long Island, New York

indicators.note: the timid person's word goes around the second in

parts.note: a mouse is a timid person

explanation.surface: On Long Island a shy man drives round in a luxury car.
explanation.definitionFit: A limousine is a large luxurious chauffeur-driven car.

clue.text: Just requirement held up without reason

parts.note: a want is a need or requirement
just means only

explanation.surface: A fair demand is delayed for no good cause.
explanation.definitionFit: To act this way is to act gratuitously, with no justification or motive.

clue.text: Dollar novel originally engraved free of charge

parts.note: a buck is a dollar
She is a novel by H. Rider Haggard

indicators.note: the opening letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A dollar bill bearing a new engraving is given away.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckshee is British slang for gratis, given for nothing.

clue.text: New arrival put out about one who's established

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about the celebrity
out here means disordered, so the word put is rearranged

parts.note: a star is someone established in their field

explanation.surface: A newcomer is upset about a veteran figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges PUT to UPT, which goes about STAR.
explanation.definitionFit: An upstart is someone who has suddenly risen in position, a parvenu.

clue.text: Coffee mother served outside old church

indicators.note: the mother word is placed outside the other pieces

parts.note: ma is mother

explanation.surface: Mum serves coffee outside an ancient chapel.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocha is a fine Arabian coffee, named after the Yemeni port.

clue.text: Officer on leave collecting son to be together

indicators.note: in a down clue the officer sits on top of the rest

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer

indicators.note: the departure word collects the son inside it

parts.note: to exit is to leave

explanation.surface: An officer on furlough picks up his son so they can be united.
explanation.definitionFit: To coexist is to live alongside one another at the same time.

clue.text: English vessel in trouble, held up in foreign port

indicators.note: the English vessel goes in the trouble word
in a down clue, held up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble
SS, steamship, is a vessel

explanation.surface: A British ship in difficulties is detained at an overseas harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Odessa is a major Black Sea port in Ukraine.

clue.text: Giant's hopelessness

definitions.meaning: Giant ... owns Doubting Castle in Bunyan's The Pilgrim's Progress
hopelessness means utter loss of hope

explanation.definitionFit: Bunyan names his giant after the state of total hopelessness.

clue.text: A puzzle upset fabulous author

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, the word read backwards

parts.note: to pose is to puzzle, as in a question that poses a problem

explanation.surface: A conundrum unsettled a wonderful writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the Greek writer of fables, hence fabulous.

clue.text: Having wealth, work fast to protect university

indicators.note: the charade wraps round the university letter to guard it

parts.note: op, opus, is a work
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: A rich person labours quickly to shield a college.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulent means rich and affluent.

clue.text: Symbols of rank displayed by sailor on board

indicators.note: on board means placed aboard, inside the ship letters

parts.note: on board a ship, SS being steamship
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: Insignia are worn by a seaman aboard ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Stars on epaulettes show officers' rank.

clue.text: Islander taking fish out East with Scotsman

indicators.note: the compass point is taken out of the fish's name

parts.note: a sardine is a fish
Ian is the Scottish form of John, a stock Scotsman's name

explanation.surface: An island man catches fish out east with a Scot.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sardinian is a native of Sardinia, a Mediterranean island.

clue.text: Method of backing favourite after Aintree start? In no way

definitions.text: Method of backing favourite after Aintree start? In no way

parts.words: Method of backing favourite after Aintree start? In no way
parts.note: a style of betting done well before the race, so never after the off at the Grand National course

explanation.surface: A punter wonders about betting on the favourite once the race has started.
explanation.walkthrough: Aintree is the Liverpool racecourse of the Grand National. The bet is placed in advance: Latin ante means before, and post is the starting post.
explanation.definitionFit: Ante-post betting is wagering on a race days ahead, before the runners are declared.

clue.text: Grand appearance of aristocracy

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand
an entry is an appearance, as of an actor on stage

explanation.surface: Nobility makes a magnificent entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: The gentry are the upper classes, landed families just below the nobility.
